title: The Guardian To Offer ‘NAZA’ For Free On Website From November After Theatrical Run & Is Exploring Ways To Show Doc In Israel & Palestinian Territories
text:
The Guardian and mk2 films have announced global release plans for Israeli directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor ’s bombshell documentary NAZA .

The partners said that The Guardian-produced documentary will be released theatrically from September 28 onwards in more than 50 territories, having secured theatrical distributors in 56 territories since its world premiere at the Venice Film Festival on September 10, where it went on to win the Special Jury Prize.

In an unprecedented move, The Guardian will make NAZA available for global audiences for free on its website, after the theatrical run from late November. The partners said the move was due to the “worldwide interest” in the documentary as well as The Guardian’s “commitment to fearless, independent journalism”. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Neon Joins Yuval Abraham & Rachel Szor's Explosive Gaza-Israel Doc 'NAZA' News Curtain Up: 'La Bola Negra' Shines As Netflix Shares Grosses In Historic First -- Specialty Box Office

The investigative documentary, exposing the Israeli military ‘s calculated targeting of civilians in Gaza in missile strikes through the testimony of intelligence personnel and soldiers involved in the killing, has caused a sensation since its Venice debut.

It landed a record 25-minute ovation its Venice premiere Film , but has since been attacked by Israeli politicians including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has threatened to strip the directors of their Israeli citizenship even though he has no power to do this under the country’s laws.

The Guardian and mk2 said the film has been offered to a number of distributors and cinemas in Israel , and they will be exploring other ways to enable the film to be seen in the occupied Palestinian territories.

They added that, as previously announced, the film will receive its North American premiere on 26 September at New York Film Festival, and will open in U.S. theaters on September 30, launching exclusively at the IFC Center in New York City.

It will expand to Los Angeles and other key markets on October 9, ahead of a national roll out in the weeks to follow.

NAZA is produced by The Guardian and James Wilson (JW Films); and executive produced by Oscar-winning filmmaker Jonathan Glazer.

The documentary builds on a series of revelations first published by the Guardian, +972 Magazine, a Israeli-Palestinian publication, and Hebrew-language outlet, Local Call between 2023-2025, including groundbreaking investigations into how Israel uses AI to identify targets in Gaza.

It follows Abraham and Szor’s No Other Land , winner of the Best Documentary Academy Award in 2025. Co-directed with Palestinian filmmakers Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal, it documented Israeli army-backed efforts to erase the West Bank Palestinian villages of Masafer Yatta, while painting a wider picture of Israeli occupation.

“We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israelis to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible,” said Abraham and Szor in a joint statement as the NAZA release plans were unveiled.

“The threats from the Israeli government to revoke our citizenship and the death threats do not change that and will not stop the film. We thank our colleagues for the solidarity and look forward to sharing NAZA all over the world very soon.”

Harry Davies, a Guardian investigations correspondent and one of NAZA’s producers, added: “ NAZA is grounded in rigorous journalism published over the past three years, but it is also a powerful piece of cinema that will soon be available on screens, large and small, around the world.” “The initial response from those who’ve seen it shows audiences are engaging deeply with the urgent questions the film raises. We’re working with MK2 and international partners to bring the film to global audiences as soon as possible.”

The 56 territories sold by Paris-based mk2 film, which boarded international sales on the documentary ahead of its Venice premiere, include France, UK, Italy, Spain, Germany, Belgium, Netherlands, Austria, Switzerland, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Greece, Portugal, Poland, Lithuania, Romania, Bulgaria, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Thailand, Canada, Brazil, Turkey, Central America, and the Middle East.

title: ParaBros Merger Settlement Sign-Off Delayed As Deal Foes Granted Hail Mary Move By Judge
text:
Mere hours before a court hearing on the much criticized settlement between Paramount and a coalition of blue state attorneys general on the $111 billion merger with Warner Bros Discovery, ParaBros foes have gained a victory that could see an expensive delay on the deal closing.

“The Court GRANTS the administrative motions to file amicus briefs,” U.S. District Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin just ruled on Block the Merger ‘s Administrative motion filed earlier today . “All amicus briefs must be filed on the docket by no later than 12:01 a.m. PST on September 25, 2026. This deadline will not be extended, and tardy submissions will not be considered.”

RELATED: Trump DOJ Official Minimizes State AGs’ Paramount-WBD Settlement, Says It Yielded No New Antitrust-Related Commitments Watch on Deadline

With an 11 a.m. PT virtual hearing before Martinez-Olguin widely viewed as a rubberstamping of the September 21 antitrust settlement and hence the mega-merger itself, the granting of Block the Merger’s move makes it almost certain the deal won’t be formally approved today.

“We are pleased that the court is allowing the public to weigh in on this important issue because the AGs have failed to adequately represent the public interest in this case,” Free Press Co-CEO and BTM co-counsel Jessica J. González told Deadline after the motion was granted. “The consent decree is weak and unenforceable. We look forward to explaining that in further detail in our brief due at midnight tonight.”

The League of United Latin American Citizens has also been granted its request to to file an amicus brief in the ParaBros settlement.

As it stands, the settlement hearing is still on the court calendar with Judge Martinez-Olguin likely to have questions of California AG Rob Bonta ‘s team along with Beth Wilkinson and Ellison’s other lawyers.

RELATED: Post-Merger Paramount May Overdeliver On Settlement Terms With 36-Film 2027 Slate Amid Speculation About Duplication & WB Leadership

That’s a prospect — as my colleague Ted Johnson noted earlier today — that already had Paramount seeing red this morning with fears of being forced “to incur tens (if not hundreds) of millions of dollars of payments while adding nothing to the record.”

“Any briefing and comment process that would enable non-parties to delay the closing of this transaction—inflicting massive harm on Paramount—without filing their own antitrust action, making the showing required under the Clayton Act to obtain preliminary injunctive relief, or posting a bond to protect Defendants from the harm caused by such delay would be improper,” said an opposition filing by the David Ellson-run company and WBD this morning. The opposition came before the Judge made her ruling granting the amicus briefs. “Such an unprecedented process would unravel the carefully calibrated protections of the Clayton Act and place non-parties in a superior position to parties seeking to halt a merger.”

RELATED: Paramount To Keep Headquarters In Los Angeles Post-Merger: “We Aren’t Going Anywhere”

To that, after Ellison proclaimed earlier this week he envisioned the merger coming together in the next two weeks , Paramount again finds itself looking at a $7 million-a-day ticking fee to WBD shareholders beginning on October 1.

The threat of those fees, which add up to more than $630 million a quarter, was central to Paramount’s much-leaked threat to exit California for a red state like Tennessee if the ParaBros merger was nixed or had to wait for the outcome of a trial set to start March 2. In fact, outside of the talks this past Yom Kippur weekend between CA AG Bonta and Team Paramount to work out a settlement, the parties originally were set to meet today in court for a hearing on Ellison’s bid for a $1.88 billion bond to offset the “extraordinary losses” the legal battle could cost the company and the son of Oracle founder and Donald Trump buddy Larry Ellison.

RELATED: Trump Celebrity Supporters: Famous Folks In Favor Of The 47th President

Worries about job losses and economic downturns in already-ailing Hollywood saw Gov. Gavin Newsom , re-election-seeking L.A. Mayor Karen Bass, gubernatorial front-runner Xavier Becerra, IATSE and others publicly urging Bonta to resolve the standoff ASAP in the boardroom, not the courtroom (to paraphrase Bonta). Privately, even with layoffs looming once the companies are merged, the ambitious Democrats were wobbly kneed in this corporate game of chicken that MAGA-friendly Ellison would leave them holding the bag jut before the midterms.

RELATED: List Of Hollywood & Media Layoffs From Paramount To Warner Bros Discovery To CNN & More

On the other side, BTM was backed up by a legion of congressional Democrats over the weekend as settlement talks went up and down. That support was seen again today with Sen. Cory Booker (D-NJ) sending a letter to Judge Martinez-Olguin urging “the Court to subject the proposed consent decree to an independent public-interest review before entering it.” The past presidential candidate added: “The Court should measure the proposed remedies against the relief the States originally sought: an injunction blocking the merger altogether. The decree does not address the core of the case—that the merger is anticompetitive and will eliminate jobs.”

RELATED: Cory Booker Slams Paramount-WBD Merger Settlement But Blames Company And DOJ, Not State AGs

As press-savvy Booker jumped back into the ParaBros into the spotlight, Rob Bonta was on another media tour this week defending the settlement that several of his fellow AGs in the initial July 13 field antitrust suit had reservations about. To that, the AG’s office were silent Thursday on the granting of Block the Merger’s eleventh-hour motion. Paramount had nothing to say either after the motion was granted but made its POV clear in its own filing this morning.

“The proposed consent decree here is both procedurally and substantively fair,” Paramount’s opposition filing declared of the settlement that sets an oversight board of CNN and CBS News, and not much more.

RELATED: Paramount-WBD Settlement Sets Up Editorial Independence Board For CNN And CBS News

“Twelve state attorneys general and Defendants reached an arm’s length agreement after extensive and difficult negotiations, resolving the litigation risk that each side faced,” Paramount’s lawyers insist “All parties involved were represented by sophisticated and competent counsel. As described in the parties’ joint motion, the proposed consent decree ‘includes significant relief in each of the three relevant markets alleged in the Complaint.’ The fact that non-parties would have preferred different terms or a different resolution does not change this analysis, particularly because the proposed consent decree only binds the parties that consented to it.”

See ya in the midnight hour.

RELATED: Kara Swisher Says She’s Leaving CNN Now That Settlement Clears Way For Paramount-WBD Merger

title: No ParaBros Decision Today As Judge Delays Settlement Sign-Off; CA AG’s Office Insists Deal “Not The Result Of Collusion”
text:
Although David Ellison has given a lot of money to Democrats over the years, the Paramount CEO is probably not donating a dime to Sen. Cory Booker ‘s next campaign.

The much disparaged state Attorneys General-negotiated settlement in Paramount’s $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery did not receive the court approval Thursday for which Rob Bonta and Ellison had hoped.

Instead, with briefs expected by midnight tonight from opponents of the mega-merger and Paramount moving ahead with a $7.5 billon debt raise, Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin told the assembled attorneys in a hearing today that she wanted them to address by September 29 concerns raised against the deal earlier Wednesday by longtime merger foe Booker (D-NJ).

Stressing “I’ll get you a ruling in due course” (and probably stressing out Ellison as a $7 million-a-day ticking fee looms beginning October 1), the U.S. District judge also had some questions today – a lot of questions. Watch on Deadline

Addressing a screen full of top firm lawyers and state AG officials during the virtual hearing, Martinez-Olguin wanted to know if the settlement and the consent decree actually “addresses the Clayton Act concerns” that were in the July 13 antitrust suit Bonta, New York’s Letitia James, and 10 other blue-state AGs filed against the merger. With the sharp realpolitiks at play from California Gov. Gavin Newsom and others for a settlement, Martinez-Olguin also had concerns that the roller-coaster deal was “not the result of collusion and was more of an arm’s length process.”

Her blunt words clearly landed hard with her immediate audience of attorneys (and maybe the more than 640 others on the Zoom).

Even before the judge issued her “homework” for the lawyers, the California Senior Assistant AG Paula Blizzard argued for the settlement while at the same time dismissing Paramount’s “threats” and “blackmail” to “pull out of California.” However, claiming the states were still prepared to take the whole matter to trial starting March 2, 2027 if the consent degree wasn’t approved, Blizzard also acknowledged the backlash the settlement has received over the past 72 hours since it was unveiled on Monday morning.

“We absolutely recognize that this merger has engendered a large amount of controversy and commentary and feelings and concerns on a whole host of issues,” she said near the end of the nearly one-hour session. “A lot of these are outside antitrust,” Blizzard added. “They reflect the country’s very broad political and philosophical divides, concerns about the state of the news media, people’s relationship to big companies and consolidation and corporate power, and we hear those voices, we listen to those voices, we respect those voices. But at the end of the day, this is an antitrust case, and it is focused on the antitrust law.”

Booker’s six-page letter to the judge Wednesday asked for her to “subject the proposed consent decree to an independent public-interest review before entering it.” Paramount filed paperwork of its own Wednesday, just before the virtual hearing, essentially telling the Garden State senator to mind his own business.

During today’s hearing, Blizzard appeared to address Booker’s concerns without saying his name.

Insisted the deal was “presumptively valid,” she told Martinez-Olguin it was the result of a final surge of talks over “tens of hours, in-person video conferences, phone conferences, drafts-all the normal things you would see in a consent decree, except magnified because you had 12 attorneys general on our side.” It should be noted, New Jersey was one of the states in the ParaBros antitrust gang, and their AG Jennifer Davenport agreed to the settlement announced September 21.

Aware his bosses were watching, Paramount outside counsel Josh Holiann made a point of disputing the use of the term ” blackmail” when it came to timed leaks the Ellisons were serious about pulling up Melrose lot stakes, jobs and productions to redder jurisdictions (“It was a business decision …Paramount had to make.”). In a less defensive posture, the Latham & Watkins attorney also promised the judge the penalties in the settlement would now “keep our feet to the fire.”

Still, With Para and WBD lawyers Holian, Beth Wilkinson, Jeffrey Kessler, Daniel Petrocelli and Marguerite Sullivan  on-screen (some clearly working on something else), it was mainly Blizzard who took point trying to sell Martinez-Olguin on the deal — and it sure seemed like a hard sell.

“We believe we have five years of remedies that will remove the competitive concerns we see the harms we see and preserve competition,” Blizzard said. With nodded agreement from Paramount attorneys, Blizzard stressed the divestment of some cable channels if necessary and Miramax and other clauses in the settlement is “the best solution” other than blocking “it completely?”

Sounding very much like she was arguing for Paramount, Blizzard ventured into some hard Hollywood realities to give the deal context. “Obviously, in this case, Warner Bros originally said it was going to sell its assets,” Blizzard said. “So, if we block this merger, there will probably be another one, perhaps before Your Honor, in a year or so, and is that the best solution for the markets to preserve the competition that the Clayton Act requested.”

Kneecapped to some extent by Zoom-wide technical glitches that initially prevented some of the attorneys and state government officials from participating in the virtual hearing, the hearing on the now delayed settlement sign-off was delayed itself by nearly 15 minutes.

Now, with that ticking fee clock ticking, ParaBros closure is also once again delayed — at least until Monday at noon. Well played Sen. Booker.

title: ‘Minions & Monsters’ Sets Peacock Release Date
text:
Minions & Monsters will begin streaming on Peacock on October 28, following its July 1 theatrical release.

Starring Pierre Coffin, Allison Janney, Christoph Waltz, Jesse Eisenberg, Jeff Bridges and Zoey Deutch, the seventh installment in the Despicable Me franchise and third in the Minions prequel series is set in 1920s Hollywood. As Deadline’s Damon Wise noted in his review, the opening credits alone trace the history of the Universal logo back to the silent-era days of The Trans-Atlantic Film Company. Per the synopsis, the Illumination /Universal film tells “the rambunctious, ridiculous and totally true story” of how the Minions — led by Dick — conquered Hollywood, became movie stars, lost everything, unleashed monsters onto the world and then banded together to try and save the planet from the mayhem they had just created. Related Stories News 'The Mummy' Movie Reteaming Brendan Fraser And Rachel Weisz Gets A Title News NBCU's Donna Langley On Industry Mergers, Taylor Sheridan, And The Road to 2027

The latest installment is directed by Oscar nominee Pierre Coffin, who helmed the first three Despicable Me films and the first Minions movie. Coffin also provides the voice of the Minions in the film, which he has done since the characters’ film debut in 2010. Watch on Deadline

Brian Lynch ( Minions , The Secret Life of Pets films) and Coffin wrote the screenplay, which is produced by Illumination’s Oscar-nominated founder and CEO Chris Meledandri and Bill Ryan ( The Super Mario Bros. Movie) . Lynch also is an EP.

Minions & Monsters was a box office success, grossing $524 million worldwide and becoming the ninth-highest-grossing globally for 2026.

Created 15 years ago, the Minions have boosted Illumination’s Despicable Me and Minions to a global box office of more than $5.6 billion. The previous Minions film, 2022’s Minions: The Rise of Gru , was a summer tentpole, earning almost $1 billion worldwide.

title: ‘Kaali Kheti’, Horror Starring Jackie Shroff, Sharad Kelkar and Neha Sargam, Sets Indian Release Date
text:
EXCLUSIVE: Jackie Shroff , Sharad Kelkar and Neha Sargam are starring in eerie Indian rural horror Kaali Kheti , which has been given a domestic theatrical release date of October 23.

Above and below you can see a poster for the pic, which has been quietly shooting with Haris Imtiyaz Khan the writer and director. Sana Khan is the producer, with BlackCanvas Studio the production house in association with Zeroland Production.

Virendra Saxena and Shaji Choudhary appear alongside veteran actor Shroff, Kelkar and Sargam. Related Stories News Prime Video Adds Sony LIV To Indian Offer News The "Algorithm Breaking" 'Hunkkaar' Has Challenged Indian Audiences On The Limits Of Procedural TV - And Their Own Beliefs

Per the synopsis, Kaali Kheti is “set against a rural backdrop and explores a world where family, legacy and buried truths come together to create an unsettling tale of fear.” The plot is remaining under wraps with producers keen to keep “audiences guessing about what the film is truly about.” Watch on Deadline

Director Khan said: “For me Kaali Kheti is about examining agriculture through the lens of horror. Something I hadn’t seen before. Something that felt fresh, exciting and also deeply disturbing. The film is mirror to society, only the reflection exists in a scary and fantastical world. Sometimes this world doesn’t make sense but always feels strangely familiar. Perhaps that is the true horror.”

Produced under the banner of BlackCanvas Studio, the film brings together an ensemble cast led by Jackie Shroff and Sharad Kelkar, with Neha Sargam, Virendra Saxena and Shaji Choudhary in pivotal roles.

title: ‘Game Of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest’ Movie Gets 2029 Release Date
text:

No cast or production start info yet.

The movie reportedly centers on, you guessed it, Aegon I, the first Lord of the Seven Kingdoms, who spawned the Targaryen dynasty — the royal family at the heart of the entire franchise. Aegon I the Conquerer founded and is the first king of the dynasty and united Westeros with his dragons Balerion, Vhagar and Meraxes.

This would mark the first time Aegon I has been depicted onscreen. The feature is an expansion of George R.R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire. Watch on Deadline

Aside from the core HBO franchise, there are two spinoff series based on Martin’s fantasy novels: House of the Dragon and A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms .

title: Curry Barker’s Next Movie ‘Anything But Ghosts’ Sets May 2027 Release From Focus Features
text:
Curry Barker fever will continue into next summer as Focus Features and Blumhouse Atomic Monster are releasing the Obsession filmmaker’s next movie, Anything but Ghosts on May 7.

That’s similar to the launch date of Obsession, which bowed during the third weekend of May this year (May 15). It opened to $17.1M domestic , but held like a rock, spiking an unprecedented 39% in its second weekend ($23.9M) and another 14% in its third weekend with $27.3M for a final domestic tally of$263.4M and nearly $520M worldwide.

As we first told you, Focus has worldwide rights on Anything but Ghosts, with Universal Pictures International handling international distribution for the studio. Barker co-wrote the movie with his longtime creative collaborator and Obsession star Cooper Tomlinson. Anything but Ghosts stars Tomlinson and Barker as wannabe “ghosthunters” who find themselves in over their heads as things spiral wildly and terrifyingly out of control. Violet McGraw and Chris Reinacher also star with Bryce Dallas Howard and Aaron Paul. Barker  has saidin interviews that the feature takes place in the same universe as Obsession.

RELATED: ‘Game Of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest’ Movie Gets 2029 Release Date

Already opening on May 7 next year is Lionsgate’s Mel Gibson-directed The Resurrection of the Christ (Part One) — technically that’s going on May 6 — as well as 20th Century Studios’ Patrick Schwarzenegger-Phoebe Dynevor movie Beach Read . Sony kicks off summer 2027 on April 30 with the feature take on Nintendo video game The Legend of Zelda.

The other production companies on Anything but Ghosts are Spooky Pictures, Divide/Conquer, in association with Image Nation and Barker and Tomlinson’s That’s a Bad Idea. EPs are Daniel Bekerman, Barker, Tomlinson and Ben Ross. Producers are Roy Lee, Steven Schneider, Jason Blum, Adam Hendricks and Greg Gilreath.

Focus Features acquired Obsession out of TIFF Midnight Madness 2025 for $15M. CAA Media Finance sold the film, which went on to become Focus’ highest-grossing movie ever in addition to being the highest-grossing movie ever acquired out of a film festival (unseating The Blair Witch Project ‘s $248.6M WW gross). Barker’s debut feature, Milk & Serial, first streamed on YouTube to close to 3M views off a production budget of $800. Obsession was made for $750K by Capstone Studios before Focus picked up the title.

Barker mentioned to Deadline at our DGA TIFF panel that on Anything but Ghosts, “The hardest day on Obsession was the easiest day on Anything but Ghosts .”

He added: “We had a 130-page script, and we had 26 days to shoot it. I’m also starring in it and directing and I’m the lead character. I have more lines than anyone in the movie. Zach Kregger just told me, ‘You have to cut 30 pages,’ and I probably should have listened to him. So did my manager; he told me that, too.

“But I didn’t cut a single page because I wanted to shoot all of it,” added Barker, who was at TIFF for the one-year anniversary of the Obsession premiere. “It was the hardest thing I’ve ever done, and we were compromising shots left and right off the shot list. Gone. Just like coverage was going out the windows. It was crazy.”

title: ‘KPop Demon Hunters 2’ Targeting “A Very Broad Theatrical Release,” Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos Says, Addressing Streamer’s Distribution Strategy
text:
KPop Demon Hunters has broken streaming records for Netflix , amassing 325.1M views in its first 90 days on the platform and spending 63 consecutive weeks in the Global Top 10. The direct-to-streaming animated Sony title showed a massive box-office potential too — two months after KPop Demon Hunters ‘ debut on Netflix, its singalong version grossed estimated $19M over just two days at No. 1, with all circuits playing it except AMC which had boycotted Netflix in the past over its reluctance to commit to a 45-day theatrical window.

Not surprisingly, Netflix is planning a “big, broad, global” theatrical release for the sequel to the family smash, expected in 2029 , the streamer’s co-CEO Ted Sarandos revealed at Bloomberg’s Screentime Wednesday night while discussing Netflix’s evolving theatrical release strategy.

Upcoming movies that will hit theaters first before launching on Netflix include Cannes Best Director winner La Bola Negra (Oct. 16) , Peter Berg’s Mosquito Bowl (Oct. 30) , David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth (Nov. 25) , Danny Boyle’s Ink (Dec. 11) , Greta Gerwig’s Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew (Feb. 12, 2027) and animated title Charlie vs. the Chocolate Factory (Nov. 5, 2027). Watch on Deadline

“On one end of the spectrum is La Bola Negra, Train Dreams last year that could have played in the theaters for six months and it wouldn’t have impacted, it would have done net positive on Netflix,” Sarandos said. “Those kind of art house films play like that. And then the other end is the kind of four-quad family rewatch movie, so we said let’s take those two and treat them different. We’re going to do a big wide release for Narnia next year, and then we’ll do a big wide release for Charlie vs. the Chocolate Factory at the end of the year. We think they’ll do great, and when the KPop Demon Hunters sequel comes, you can expect a very broad theatrical release.”

Narnia, Charlie and La Bola Negra are getting 50, 47 and 46-day theatrical window, respectively; for Cliff Booth and Mosquito Bowl , it’s 27 and 26, respectively.

On those movies, Netflix will also report boxoffice for the first time. What would the streamer consider a success for a film first released in theaters?

“It won’t be tied to the P&L itself, relatively low expectations that will add much to the financial outcome of the film itself,” Sarandos said. “If you’re gonna say, pick a little risk to the Netflix performance, it should have the potential for a very big upside in the theater. So, for Narnia , for KPop Demon Hunters , that’s why they’re gonna get big, broad, global release. But I think in the other ones where it’s kind of in the middle, that’s where it gets tougher.”

Sarandos noted that the most watched movies of all time on the platform are Netflix originals, beating pay-TV window titles, “except for the kids and family movies because they get a lot of rewatching.”

For the rest, boxoffice success does not necessarily translate into streaming success.

“No disparaging movies in the boxoffice, but movies that come out in the theater do pretty well, what happens is the most passionate audience went to see it in the theater, so by the time it comes to Netflix, you’ve lost that passionate audience, and you got the people that go, ‘Oh, I meant to see that,’ or ‘I’ll get around to that.'”

Sarandos said that last year, Netflix put over 30 movies in the theaters for various periods of time, keeping some on the big screen after its streaming release, including Frankenstein, which stayed in theaters for six months.

title: Francis Coppola’s ‘Megalopolis’ Back In Theaters
text:
EXCLUSIVE : For the first time since its 2024 launch, Francis Ford Coppola’s Megalopolis will return to theaters in a limited engagement that will allow audiences to interact with the iconic director.

Coppola decided when he self-financed and shot the provocative film that it would not be put through any domestic-based streaming services or DVDs produced for the U.S. market. He felt it was now time to put it back out.

Reading International Inc. has booked the film in many its cinemas around the country, from New York to Hawaii, to screen simultaneously on October 24. Venues will include Village East Cinemas in New York City. This will be followed by a livestreamed Q&A with Coppola, moderated by his son and collaborator, Roman Coppola, who was second unit director on the picture. Audience members will be able to text their questions before, during and after the film. The filmmaker will answer the best ones live during the presentation.

“ Megalopolis is back in its rightful place, theaters, and the interest in seeing it as was intended is growing,” said Coppola. “I am excited to take part in an interactive Q&A across multiple theaters simultaneously.” Watch on Deadline

RELATED: Francis Ford Coppola Reveals The Movie He Is Most Proud Of … The Answer May Surprise

Coppola spent a fortune to personally stake a film that became one of the most expensive indies ever, one he’d been dreaming about for decades. Much the way that audiences continue to discover his other films, Coppola hoped Megalopolis would follow a similar track, and that it will be viewed and debated long after he has passed away. He believes its themes of rebuilding cities and the polarizing political factions will be continually relevant. The film’s ensemble cast is headed by Adam Driver, Shia LaBeouf, Dustin Hoffman, Jon Voight, Nathalie Emmanuel, Laurence Fishburne, Aubrey Plaza and Giancarlo Esposito.

Each screening also will include hard-copy letters from Coppola given to each audience member, containing his official director’s statement about Megalopolis for audience members to read before watching the film. Each screening will also include the famed unique “Live Element,” which was only available at select screenings when the film was first released.

Megalopolis will find its way back in theaters periodically going forward, including the tradition of the film screening at multiple theaters every New Year’s Day. This fulfills a wish from Coppola to have the film be shown on this day as a symbol of coming together and discussing ideas for improvement as a society.

title: ‘VisionQuest’ Release Schedule: When Do New Episodes Arrive?
text:
The third and final installment of the WandaVision universe, VisionQuest , will focus on Paul Bettany ’s synthetic superhero.

First introduced cinematically in Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015), Vision was created by placing J.A.R.V.I.S. (also voiced by Paul Bettany) into a Vibranium body that villain Ultron (James Spader) intended to inhabit, with the help of the Mind Stone.

VisionQuest will see him return following the events of WandaVision , which picked up after the character’s tragic death in Avengers: Infinity War (2018) when Thanos killed him to complete his gauntlet with the Mind Stone.

Find release rollout details for Marvel ’s VisionQuest below: Watch on Deadline

When does VisionQuest come out?

Marvel’s VisionQuest arrives on the small screen Wednesday, October 14.

How many episodes are in VisionQuest ? Will new episodes arrive weekly or all at once?

There will be eight episodes in the latest MCU television installment. It will premiere with the first two episodes, and release two episodes per week for the following two weeks before the penultimate episode and finale arrive one per week in November. See the full release rollout, complete with episode titles, below:

What is VisionQuest about?

Rebooted and hiding out after escaping those who aimed to use him as a weapon, Vision searches for purpose by consulting F.R.I.D.A.Y., E.D.I.T.H., J.A.R.V.I.S. and Ultron, all of the AI personas embedded into his programming. A bounty placed on his head threatens his existence lying low and sends him on the run with the mysterious Thomas Shepherd (Ruaridh Mollica), who might be Vision’s son reincarnate and brother to Joe Locke’s Billy Maximoff, formerly Billy Kaplan. Vision must get to the root of Thomas’ identity while resisting Ultron’s influence, evading capture and confronting his true nature.

title: ‘Lizard Music’ Starring Dwayne Johnson And Directed By Benny Safdie To Tune Up Christmas Day 2027 Via Amazon MGM
text:
EXCLUSIVE: Amazon MGM Studios has set the theatrical release date for the live-action/CGI hybrid Lizard Music , starring Dwayne Johnson and directed by Benny Safdie, for December 25, 2027.

Lizard Music follows a boy (Theo Clark Leber) left to his own devices who stumbles upon a secret late-night broadcast of lizards playing otherworldly music, and a hidden door to the extraordinary swings open. His search for answers leads him to an eccentric and whimsical old man nicknamed The Chicken Man (Johnson) and his beloved companion, an 85-year-old chicken named Claudia – the boy and the old man become kindred spirits who find each other at just the right time. United by a shared vision, they set off on an adventure that begins as a hunt for a hidden society but blossoms into something far greater: a voyage through invisible worlds, unexpected harmonies, and the unbreakable bond between lost souls who discover magic not only in what they find, but also in each other. Watch on Deadline

The project is billed as being another transformative role for Johnson, with extensive makeup and prosthetics used to turn him into the eccentric septuagenarian Chicken Man. Alicia Silverstone, Tim Heidecker, Arya Parvathi, Regina Hall, Colman Domingo, Jeff Goldblum, Rachel McAdams, Andrew Dice Clay and David Krumholtz also star.

Safdie adapted the screenplay off Daniel Pinkwater’s novel of the same name. Producers include UA’s Scott Stuber and Nick Nesbitt, Out for the Count Productions’ Safdie, Seven Bucks Productions’ Johnson, and Magnetic Fields Entertainment’s David Koplan.

Given the fantasy and wonder nature of the project, a Christmas launchpad is ideal in reaching family audiences. Lizard Music will arrive in theaters next year following the December 17 release of Disney/Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Secret Wars, New Line’s Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum and Lionsgate’s sequel The Housemaid’s Secret.

Also opening on Christmas Day 2027 so far are Amazon MGM Studios’ Ron Howard-directed actioner Alone at Dawn starring Adam Driver and Anne Hathaway , and a Warner Bros’ movie being directed by Nancy Meyers.
